_meta.note: Structured choice/state graph for all 40 choices in CHOICES.md. This is the mechanical structure (options, skill/flag effects, gates) — NOT the narrative prose for each scene, which is separate, larger authoring work not yet done. See STATE_MODEL.md for how this data drives divergence and endings.

choices.title: Which teacher to seek out first

options.label: Rigorous scholastic training first
options.detail: The madrasa route means years under recognized teachers, learning the tradition's own internal logic before you're trusted to argue past it. It is slower, and it costs you nothing in reputation — orthodox training is never held against a scholar later. But it also means that if you ever do reach the unconventional teachers, you'll arrive already shaped by exactly the system they exist to challenge.

options.label: Seek unconventional teachers immediately
options.detail: Going straight to the fringe teachers means faster access to real, dangerous knowledge, and it signals real seriousness to the people who matter most in that world. It also means skipping the credentialing that protects a scholar later — when rivals eventually call your system heretical, you won't have an orthodox pedigree to point to as cover.

choices.title: How openly to align with Akhlati

options.label: Declare discipleship openly
options.detail: Declaring yourself Akhlati's disciple openly announces exactly where your intellectual loyalties lie. It earns you standing with everyone who respects him — and it means his enemies, and any future inquisitors, will always know exactly where to start when building a case against you.

options.label: Study quietly, keep it deniable
options.detail: Studying quietly costs you nothing in the short term: no one can prove the association, and your options stay open. But knowledge half-hidden is knowledge half-trusted — teachers notice students who won't stand behind them, and it can cost you the depth of instruction reserved for those who commit visibly.

choices.title: How to treat the friendship with Yazdi

options.label: Collaborate as equals
options.detail: Treating Yazdi as a genuine intellectual partner rather than a subordinate means the two of you build something together neither could alone — real collaboration, real trust, a bond that could matter enormously later. It also means surrendering some of the authority a master normally keeps, and trusting someone still young with the full shape of your thinking.

options.label: Mentor him at arm's length
options.detail: Keeping Yazdi at a respectful, structured distance protects your authority and keeps the relationship legible to everyone watching — a teacher and his promising student, nothing more complicated. It's safer, and it costs you the kind of deep, load-bearing friendship that could carry your legacy forward if your own path goes wrong.

choices.title: How close to stand with Qasim-i Anvar

options.label: Bond deeply as fellow-travelers
options.detail: Bonding deeply with Qasim-i Anvar means real solidarity — someone who will stand with you when it's costly to do so, and you for him. It also means your fates become entangled: whatever risk his lettrist associations carry, you now share it too.

options.label: Keep a respectful distance
options.detail: Keeping Qasim-i Anvar at a respectful distance is the cautious, self-protective choice — his troubles, when they come, won't automatically become yours. But it also forgoes the kind of bond that might matter later, when you need someone who won't abandon you either.

choices.title: Which lineage to foreground

options.label: Commit to Ibn 'Arabi's tradition
options.detail: Foregrounding Ibn 'Arabi alone aligns you with the tradition's most famous, most argued-over authority — instant legitimacy with everyone who already reveres him, and instant target status with anyone who considers him controversial.

options.label: Elevate Hamuya instead
options.detail: Elevating Hamuya over the far more famous Ibn 'Arabi is the bolder, riskier claim — you're betting your own judgment against the tradition's settled hierarchy of who matters, in front of readers who may never have even heard Hamuya's name.

options.label: Insist on both (the historical choice)
options.detail: Insisting on both traditions at once, the historical choice, commits you to a harder synthesis and pleases no faction's partisans completely. It is also the intellectually honest position — and the one most likely to be remembered as genuinely original rather than merely derivative.

choices.title: Accept patronage at all

options.label: Accept the court appointment
options.detail: Accepting the court appointment buys you security, resources, and a stage — but it also ties your fortunes to Iskandar Sultan's own, for better or worse. If his star falls, you may fall with it.

options.label: Remain independent
options.detail: Staying unaffiliated means no one owns your time or your doctrine — you write and teach exactly as you see fit. It also means going without patronage's protection and its purse, in a world where an unattached scholar is an unprotected one.

choices.title: How much doctrine to reveal to Iskandar Sultan

options.label: Present the full, still-forming system
options.detail: Presenting your full, still-forming system to a young prince is a bet that his curiosity outweighs his caution — it can win you a patron who genuinely understands and champions the work, not just funds it. It also means he now knows exactly how far your thinking goes, which he may repeat, misremember, or someday use against you.

options.label: A court-palatable, watered-down version
options.detail: Offering a safer, court-palatable version protects you from early exposure and keeps the prince comfortable. It also means he never really knows what he's patronizing — and doors that require his genuine understanding, later, may simply not open.

choices.title: Align with the atelier's artists, or stand apart

options.label: Collaborate with poets and painters
options.detail: Joining the atelier's poets and painters means your ideas start absorbing their instincts — image, rhythm, spectacle — which can make your work more vivid and more widely felt. It also blurs the line between philosopher and courtier, a line some colleagues will later use against your seriousness.

options.label: Keep to philosophy and law
options.detail: Keeping to philosophy and law preserves your reputation as a serious thinker, untouched by the atelier's more decorative reputation. It also means missing whatever cross-pollination might have sharpened your own ideas, and staying a little apart from the court's most influential circle.

choices.title: React to the first flicker of rival jealousy

options.label: Flaunt the theory to build reputation fast
options.detail: Flaunting the theory builds your reputation fast — more students, more attention, more standing at court, right when you need it. It also broadcasts exactly what a jealous rival needs to know, years before you're ready to defend it.

options.label: Introduce it cautiously
options.detail: Introducing the idea cautiously keeps you safer for longer — word spreads by reputation rather than declaration, with little for a rival to seize on directly. It also means slower growth, and risks others claiming credit for ideas you were too careful to attach your name to loudly.

choices.title: Loyalty through political risk

options.label: Stay loyal to Iskandar Sultan through the downturn
options.detail: Staying loyal through Iskandar Sultan's decline is a bet on gratitude — if he remembers who stood with him, that debt could matter enormously later. It is also a bet against the odds: falling patrons rarely recover, and loyalty to a losing side can taint you by association.

options.label: Quietly cultivate the next patron early
options.detail: Quietly building ties to your next patron while the current one still reigns is simple self-preservation — you land safely no matter what happens to Iskandar Sultan. It also means there's no debt of loyalty left to call in later, from him or from anyone watching how you treated him.

choices.title: How to present himself anew at Baysunghur's court

options.label: Lead with manuscript-arts affinity
options.detail: Leading with a shared love of the manuscript arts speaks to Baysunghur as a craftsman first, prince second — the fastest route to his genuine personal warmth, not just his patronage.

options.label: Lead with astronomical prestige
options.detail: Leading with Samarkand's rising astronomical prestige signals ambition and relevance to the wider Timurid project — impressive, but it risks reading as political positioning rather than the personal connection calligraphy could offer.

choices.title: Whether to work on the Baysunghur Qur'an

options.label: Offer a lettrist framing for the calligraphy program
options.detail: Offering a lettrist framework for the Qur'an program embeds your doctrine into one of the most scrutinized objects this court will ever produce — permanent, prestigious, and permanently exposed to anyone later looking for evidence of unorthodox thinking.

options.label: Stay deliberately separate
options.detail: Staying deliberately apart from a project this visible protects you from that scrutiny entirely. It also forfeits the chance to leave a literal, lasting mark on the single most important manuscript this court will produce.

choices.title: Balance judiciary duties against court philosophy

options.label: Let the qadi post lapse into formality
options.detail: Letting the judgeship lapse into formality frees real time and attention for the philosophical work at its most demanding stage. It also means the post — and the legitimacy, income, and legal protection it carries — is quietly weakening under you.

options.label: Stay genuinely active on the bench
options.detail: Staying genuinely active on the bench keeps your legal standing and public reputation strong, a second source of legitimacy independent of your patron's favor. It costs hours and focus the philosophical project badly needs, especially now.

choices.title: Pursue a formal tie to the Samarkand Observatory

options.label: Actively seek association through Yazdi
options.detail: Actively seeking a formal tie to Samarkand through Yazdi could open real institutional doors — access, resources, a second base of legitimacy in the most prestigious scientific project of the age. It also costs effort and political capital chasing an association that may never fully materialize.

options.label: Stay Isfahan-rooted
options.detail: Staying Isfahan-rooted keeps your effort focused on what's already working. It also means the friendship with Yazdi carries the entire weight of that connection — powerful while it lasts, and entirely dependent on one relationship holding.

choices.title: Respond to a rival's first public challenge

options.label: Answer publicly and immediately
options.detail: Answering the challenge on the spot, in the same room, is the decisive move — it can end the argument before it spreads, and shows you're not afraid of scrutiny. It's also irreversible: whatever you say in that moment becomes the permanent public record of how you responded.

options.label: Let it pass
options.detail: Letting the challenge pass costs you nothing in the moment and denies the rival the satisfaction of a public confrontation. It also lets the accusation sit unanswered in the room, free for anyone to interpret as evidence you had no real response.

choices.title: Primary specialization

options.label: Kimiya (alchemy)
options.detail: Alchemy is the most elite and technically demanding of the five sciences — mastering it signals serious, expensive, years-deep commitment, and the kind of prestige only the most rigorous scholars command. It is also the slowest science to show results, and the one most likely to invite accusations of chasing gold rather than truth.

options.label: Limiya (talismanry)
options.detail: Talismanry — binding celestial forces to earthly ones — sits just below alchemy in prestige, demanding careful astronomical and ritual precision. It offers real, demonstrable effects sooner than alchemy does, at only slightly less elite cost.

options.label: Himiya (subjugation)
options.detail: Subjugation — compelling planets and jinn through rigorous invocation — is powerful and dramatic, drawing both awe and suspicion in equal measure. It is a science of command, and commanding forces others fear is never entirely safe for the one doing the commanding.

options.label: Simiya (illusionism)
options.detail: Illusionism — projecting convincing but unreal images into an observer's perception — is subtler and more dangerous than it sounds: mastering how people see is mastering how they believe, which makes you as useful to a patron as you are threatening to a rival.

options.label: Rimiya (trickery)
options.detail: Trickery is the most accessible of the five sciences, the fastest to learn and the fastest to astonish a room. It is also the least prestigious — a science that pays quickly in attention and slowly, if ever, in the deep scholarly respect the other four can eventually earn.

choices.title: Specialize narrowly or diversify

options.label: Pursue the primary science exclusively
options.detail: Committing to one science alone is the historical, harder path: total specialization, total identification with a single discipline, and no fallback if that discipline falls out of favor at court.

options.label: Diversify for steadier income
options.detail: Spreading study across several sciences means steadier income and more paths forward if any one falls out of fashion. It also means you'll likely never be the single most respected master of any one science in the room.

choices.title: Mathematical foundation first, or theurgic ambition first

options.label: Build rigorous grounding first
options.detail: Building the mathematical foundation first is slower and less immediately impressive, but it means nothing you build afterward rests on an argument you can't actually defend under real scrutiny.

options.label: Lead with bold cosmological claims
options.detail: Leading with the bold cosmological claims wins attention and patron interest fast, dazzling before it's fully proven. It also means the underlying mathematics has to catch up under pressure, in public, after the claims are already out.

choices.title: When to go public with the sensory-theory innovations

options.label: Publish early to stake the claim
options.detail: Publishing the sensory-theory breakthrough now stakes your claim to it before anyone else can — priority matters, and being first is remembered. It also means defending genuinely new, unproven ideas with a reputation not yet strong enough to absorb being wrong.

options.label: Hold back until reputation is secure
options.detail: Holding the theory back until your standing can absorb any backlash is the patient, protected choice. It also risks someone else reaching the same insight first, or the idea losing its edge by the time you finally publish it.

choices.title: When to finalize and circulate the core diagram

options.label: Publish alongside the observatory's prestige
options.detail: Circulating the core diagram alongside the observatory's own rising prestige means maximum attention at the moment attention is easiest to get. It also means less time to refine a diagram meant to summarize your entire life's work.

options.label: Take the years needed to refine privately
options.detail: Taking the years the diagram actually needs means it will be exactly as good as it should be when it finally appears. It also risks missing the specific moment when Samarkand's fame could have carried your own work further, faster.

choices.title: Register of the masterwork

options.label: Dense, elite register (the historical choice)
options.detail: Writing in the dense, demanding register the historical Investigations actually used signals total seriousness and secures the tradition's respect — at the cost of a readership small enough that most of the court will never actually understand what you built.

options.label: Aim for Kashifi-style accessibility
options.detail: Writing toward Kashifi-style accessibility means far more people can actually read and use the work — wider reach, wider influence, sooner. It also trades away some of the rigor and prestige a denser, harder text would have carried.

choices.title: Teach widely or keep the circle small

options.label: Recruit and train students broadly
options.detail: Recruiting and teaching broadly means your ideas start living in more minds than just your own — real insurance against the whole system being lost if anything happens to you. It also means less control over how faithfully those ideas get carried, and a wider circle for a hostile inquiry to eventually investigate.

options.label: Keep the New Brethren small and trusted
options.detail: Keeping the New Brethren small and vetted means tighter trust and far less exposure — fewer people who could turn against you or misrepresent the work under pressure. It also means the entire system depends on very few people surviving intact.

choices.title: Write vernacular popularizations alongside the masterwork

options.label: Produce simplified Persian versions
options.detail: Producing a simplified Persian version alongside the masterwork reaches an audience the dense Arabic original never could — real influence, real income, real popular reach. It also means the simplified version becomes, for most people, the only version of your thinking they'll ever actually encounter.

options.label: Refuse — full difficulty or nothing
options.detail: Refusing to simplify protects the work's full difficulty and its prestige among serious readers. It also cedes the popular audience entirely to whoever is willing to simplify similar material instead.

choices.title: Handle requests for simplified, practical grimoire content

options.label: Take the income and status
options.detail: Taking on the practical grimoire commission means real income and real status among a wider audience, right now, when both are useful. It also attaches your name to something far less rigorous than your actual life's work, in the eyes of anyone keeping score.

options.label: Decline, protect the work's prestige
options.detail: Declining protects the seriousness and prestige of the philosophical project from any association with cheaper, more commercial material. It also turns down income and reach you may come to miss, especially once patronage becomes less reliable.

choices.title: How fully to name his sources

options.label: Be generous crediting the tradition
options.detail: Crediting Ibn 'Arabi and Hamuya generously is the intellectually honest move, and it buys real goodwill from anyone who reveres either name. It also means some of the credit for the system's originality goes to them rather than to you.

options.label: Claim more originality than is strictly true
options.detail: Letting your own name carry more of the credit than is strictly earned reads impressively in the moment — a system that looks entirely your own invention. It is also exactly the kind of thing a rival remembers and produces as evidence, later, when your honesty is in question for other reasons.

choices.title: Accept the Chief Judge appointment at all

options.label: Take the post (the historical choice)
options.detail: Taking the Chief Judge post, the historical choice, means real income, real legal standing, and a second, more conventional form of legitimacy layered on top of your philosophical reputation. It also means a second full-time job — and a second set of rivals who resent a philosopher holding real legal power.

options.label: Decline to remain scholar-only
options.detail: Declining the judgeship keeps you a scholar-only figure, free of the bench's daily demands and its particular political dangers. It also gives up the kind of institutional legitimacy and protection the post would have provided when you needed it most.

choices.title: A defining case

options.label: Rule for the powerful patron's interest
options.detail: Ruling for the powerful party is the expedient choice — it costs you nothing today and may buy useful goodwill from people who matter. It is also the choice that quietly corrodes the exact reputation, a judge who defends the weak, that has protected you until now.

options.label: Rule for the weaker party (the historical reputation)
options.detail: Ruling for the weaker party against real political pressure is the choice the histories actually remember you making — real courage, real cost, and a reputation that follows you for the rest of your life. It also makes you a concrete enemy of whoever the powerful party answers to.

choices.title: Occult reasoning on the bench

options.label: Keep judge and occultist personas separate
options.detail: Keeping judge and occultist strictly separate protects the bench from any accusation of sorcery influencing the law. It also means the two halves of your life never reinforce each other, and the court never sees what your full method can actually do.

options.label: Let lettrist reasoning inform judicial argument
options.detail: Letting lettrist reasoning shape a judicial argument, in open court, is a genuine first — it can win the case more decisively than conventional argument alone. It also puts your occult method on the legal record, permanently, for anyone later looking for grounds to call your judgment itself unorthodox.

choices.title: A case touching a rival occultist

options.label: Show scholarly solidarity and mercy
options.detail: Extending quiet solidarity to a fellow practitioner is the humane choice, consistent with everything else you believe. It is also a matter of public record — a pattern, if anyone is ever looking for one, of a judge sympathetic to occult practitioners specifically.

options.label: Enforce orthodoxy strictly
options.detail: Enforcing the law strictly, without visible sympathy, protects you from that exact pattern. It also means condemning someone whose only real difference from you is that they got caught.

choices.title: Where peak years go

options.label: Prioritize the bench's legitimacy
options.detail: Giving the year to the bench's legitimacy keeps that second source of standing solid, right when political winds are shifting. It also means the philosophical work, at the height of your intellectual powers, simply waits.

options.label: Prioritize the philosophical writing
options.detail: Giving the year to the philosophical work at its peak means producing work that may never be equaled later. It also means the docket suffers, and with it some of the legitimacy the bench provides.

choices.title: First inquisition: mode of defense

options.label: Rigorous legal/rhetorical defense
options.detail: Mounting a rigorous legal defense on the merits alone is the harder case to build and the cleanest one to win — no debts owed, no favors spent, just the argument itself standing or falling on its own strength.

options.label: Call in patron favor
options.detail: Calling in Iskandar Sultan's old loyalty, available only if you stayed loyal through his downturn, is faster and more certain — but it spends a debt you may need again, and puts your fate visibly in someone else's hands rather than your own argument's.

options.label: Attempt both at once
options.detail: Attempting both the legal defense and the patron favor at once is the strongest possible combination — and the hardest to coordinate without one undermining the other's credibility in the tribunal's eyes.

choices.title: First inquisition: recant or hold firm

options.label: Partial, face-saving recantation
options.detail: Offering a partial, face-saving recantation, phrased so everyone can pretend it wasn't quite one, is the fastest way to end this safely. It also means living afterward with having said the words, whatever you privately still believe.

options.label: Hold every position
options.detail: Holding every position without concession, in front of people who wanted you to bend, is the harder and more expensive path. It also means nothing you actually believe gets compromised in the record — whatever this costs, it won't include that.

choices.title: Second inquisition: distance from associates, or not

options.label: Preemptively distance from Qasim-i Anvar
options.detail: Preemptively distancing yourself from Qasim-i Anvar may protect you from being tied to his troubles — but if you bonded deeply with him back in Cairo, he will feel this as exactly the betrayal it looks like.

options.label: Refuse to abandon anyone
options.detail: Refusing to abandon anyone under pressure is the loyal, principled choice, and it costs you nothing in your own conscience. It also means accepting whatever risk comes from being associated with someone the tribunal has already decided to suspect.

choices.title: Third inquisition: bend the knee

options.label: Bend — survive compromised
options.detail: Bending the knee means surviving this — diminished, your system publicly qualified, but alive to argue another day. It also means saying, out loud, in front of witnesses, something less than the whole truth of what you believe.

options.label: Hold firm (the historical choice)
options.detail: Holding firm, the historical choice, means refusing to give the tribunal what it wants, whatever that costs. It is the harder, more expensive choice — and the one more likely to be remembered as integrity rather than survival.

choices.title: Third inquisition: flee, or stand trial

options.label: Attempt to flee before judgment
options.detail: Attempting to flee before judgment is undignified and uncertain, but it keeps you alive to see what happens next — outcomes a trial verdict might foreclose entirely.

options.label: Stand and face the tribunal
options.detail: Standing to face the tribunal directly, on your own name, means whatever is said of you afterward, no one can say you weren't there when it mattered. It also means accepting whatever the tribunal decides, with no way out if the verdict goes against you.

choices.title: Destination in exile

options.label: Seek a new patron at a rival court
options.detail: Seeking a new patron at a rival court bets that your reputation still travels faster than the scandal that ended your last position. It could restore some of what you lost — or it could mean discovering the scandal arrived first.

options.label: Retreat into pure private scholarship
options.detail: Retreating into pure private scholarship, with no patron and no court, protects you from further political exposure entirely. It also means the work most likely goes as far as your own remaining years and no further.

options.label: Attempt reconciliation and return
options.detail: Attempting reconciliation and a path back toward Isfahan is the hardest and highest-risk option — real vindication if it works, and confirmation of everything your accusers said about you if it doesn't.

choices.title: Keep working, or go dark

options.label: Continue writing and teaching
options.detail: Continuing to write and teach in exile keeps the work alive and visible, which matters if you want it to survive you. It also means staying a visible, reachable target for anyone still interested in finishing what the third inquisition started.

options.label: Go silent to protect what remains
options.detail: Going quiet protects what remains of both the work and yourself from further exposure. It also means nothing new gets added to it — whatever exists now is likely all that ever will.

choices.title: Entrust the manuscripts to Yazdi

options.label: Formally entrust the papers to Yazdi
options.detail: Formally entrusting your papers to Yazdi means the work has somewhere to go no matter what happens to you now — and if you built real partnership with him back in Cairo, he's positioned to carry it forward whole, not just faithfully.

options.label: Keep them close
options.detail: Keeping the papers close protects them from any hand you don't fully trust. It also means they travel exactly as far as you do, and no further — nothing survives that you don't personally carry.

choices.note: Transmission completeness in the ending logic depends on c03: entrust+equal = full transmission, entrust+mentor = partial, keep = lost regardless of c03.

choices.title: How to face death

options.label: Reconciled and at peace
options.detail: Making peace with everything this cost doesn't undo any of it — but it may be the one operation, of everything you ever mastered, that actually matters at the end.

options.label: Embittered, railing against accusers
options.detail: Going out angry at the men who did this is not wrong, exactly — they did do this. It also means the last thing anyone remembers of you is the anger, not the work.

options.label: Defiantly triumphant
options.detail: Going out certain history will eventually agree with you is either the greatest act of faith in your life or the most accurate prediction you ever made — and you won't live to find out which.

choices.title: The final testament

options.label: A public, defiant final statement
options.detail: Leaving a public, unmistakable final statement invites condemnation from exactly the people who condemned you before — but condemnation is a form of being read, argued with, and therefore remembered.

options.label: Quiet transmission to the New Brethren only
options.detail: Leaving a quiet transmission for the New Brethren alone means no proclamation and no audience, just the work itself passed hand to hand — smaller, and much harder for anyone to burn.
